title.zh: 卷九十九 漢書1: 高祖本紀上
title.en: Volume 99 Book of Later Jin 1: Gaozu Annals 1
title.raw: 卷九十九 漢書1: 高祖本紀上 Volume 99 Book of Later Jin 1: Gaozu Annals 1

sentences.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝，姓劉氏，諱暠，本名知遠，及即位改今諱。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, Sagacious in Culture, Sacred in Martial prowess, Illustrious in Solemnity, and Filial in Piety, bore the surname Liu. His taboo name was Gao; his original name was Zhiyuan, and upon accession he adopted his present taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, styled Sagacious in Culture, Sacred in Martial prowess, Illustrious in Solemnity, and Filial in Piety, was of the Liu clan. His taboo name was Gao; he had been born Zhiyuan and took his present taboo name when he ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 其先本沙陀部人也。

translations.literal: His ancestors were originally people of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were originally of the Shatuo tribe.

sentences.zh: 四代祖諱湍，帝有天下，追尊為明元皇帝，廟號文祖，陵曰懿陵；

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor, taboo name Tuan, when the Emperor possessed the realm was posthumously honored as Emperor Mingyuan, with temple name Wenzu and mausoleum called Yiling;
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor, whose taboo name was Tuan, was posthumously honored as Emperor Mingyuan when Gaozu won the empire; his temple name was Wenzu and his mausoleum Yiling;

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：湍為東漢顯宗第八子淮陽王丙之後。）〉

translations.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties states: Tuan was a descendant of Bing, Prince of Huaiyang, the eighth son of Emperor Xianzong of the Eastern Han.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Tuan descended from Bing, Prince of Huaiyang, eighth son of Emperor Xianzong of the Eastern Han.)]

sentences.zh: 高祖母隴西李氏，追謚明貞皇后。

translations.literal: Gaozu's grandmother, Lady Li of Longxi, was posthumously given the honorific title Empress Mingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's grandmother, Lady Li of Longxi, was posthumously honored as Empress Mingzhen.

sentences.zh: 曾祖諱昂，晉贈太保，追尊為恭僖皇帝，朝號德祖，陵曰沛陵；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather, taboo name Ang, was posthumously granted Grand Guardian by Jin and honored as Emperor Gongxi, with temple name Dezu and mausoleum Peiling;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather, taboo name Ang, received a posthumous grant of Grand Guardian from Jin and was honored as Emperor Gongxi, with temple name Dezu and mausoleum Peiling;

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：懿陵、沛陵皆無陵所，遙申朝拜。）〉

translations.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties states: Yiling and Peiling both have no known tomb sites; worship was offered from afar.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Institutions of the Five Dynasties: neither Yiling nor Peiling had a known burial site; court worship was offered from afar.)]

sentences.zh: 曾祖母虢國太夫人楊氏，追謚恭惠皇后。

translations.literal: His great-grandmother, Grand Lady of Guo, Lady Yang, was posthumously given the honorific title Empress Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandmother, Grand Lady Yang of Guo, was posthumously honored as Empress Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 祖諱僎，晉贈太傅，追尊為昭獻皇帝，廟號翼祖，陵曰威陵；

translations.literal: His grandfather, taboo name Zhuan, was posthumously granted Grand Tutor by Jin and honored as Emperor Zhaoxian, with temple name Yizu and mausoleum Weiling;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather, taboo name Zhuan, received a posthumous grant of Grand Tutor from Jin and was honored as Emperor Zhaoxian, with temple name Yizu and mausoleum Weiling;

sentences.zh: 祖母魯國太夫人李氏，追謚為昭穆皇后。

translations.literal: His grandmother, Grand Lady of Lu, Lady Li, was posthumously given the honorific title Empress Zhaomu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother, Grand Lady Li of Lu, was posthumously honored as Empress Zhaomu.

sentences.zh: 皇考諱琠，事後唐武皇帝為列校，晉贈太師，追尊為章聖皇帝，廟號顯祖，陵曰肅陵；

translations.literal: His imperial father, taboo name Chuan, served Emperor Wu of Later Tang as a company commander; Jin posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor and honored him as Emperor Zhangsheng, with temple name Xianzu and mausoleum Suling;
translations.idiomatic: His father, taboo name Chuan, had served Emperor Wu of Later Tang as a company commander; Jin posthumously made him Grand Preceptor and honored him as Emperor Zhangsheng, with temple name Xianzu and mausoleum Suling;

sentences.zh: 皇妣吳國太夫人安氏，追謚章懿皇后。

translations.literal: His imperial mother, Grand Lady of Wu, Lady An, was posthumously given the honorific title Empress Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Grand Lady An of Wu, was posthumously honored as Empress Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 後以唐乾寧二年，歲在乙卯，二月四日生帝於太原。

translations.literal: Later, in the second year of Qianning of Tang, the year yimao, on the fourth day of the second month, the Emperor was born at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was born at Taiyuan on the fourth day of the second month in the second year of Qianning of Tang (899), the cyclical year yimao.

sentences.zh: 帝弱不好弄，嚴重寡言，及長，面紫色，目睛多白。

translations.literal: As a child the Emperor was frail and did not care for play; he was grave and sparing of speech. When grown, his face was purplish and the whites of his eyes were prominent.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was frail and indifferent to play, grave and sparing of words. In manhood his complexion was purplish and the whites of his eyes unusually prominent.

sentences.zh: 初事唐明宗，列於麾下。

translations.literal: He first served Emperor Mingzong of Tang and was enrolled under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service under Emperor Mingzong of Tang and was enrolled in his personal command.

sentences.zh: 明宗與梁人對柵於德勝，時晉高祖為梁人所襲，馬甲連革斷，帝輟騎以授之，取斷革者自跨之，徐殿其後，晉高祖感而壯之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong faced the Liang army behind palisades at Desheng, the Jin Emperor Gaozu was then attacked by Liang forces and the leather straps of his horse armor snapped one after another. The Emperor gave up his mount and handed it over, himself mounting one whose straps had broken, and slowly brought up the rear. The Jin Emperor Gaozu was moved and admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: At Desheng, where Mingzong faced the Liang behind palisades, the future Jin Emperor Gaozu came under Liang attack and the leather ties of his horse armor snapped in succession. Gaozu gave up his own mount for him, took a horse whose ties had already broken, and brought up the rear at an easy pace. The Jin emperor was deeply moved and impressed by his steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 明宗踐阼，晉高祖為北京留守，以帝前有護援之力，奏移麾下，署為牙門都校。

translations.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, the Jin Emperor Gaozu was military governor of the Northern Capital; because the Emperor had earlier rendered protective aid, he memorialized to transfer him under his command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong took the throne, the Jin emperor served as military governor of the Northern Capital. Remembering Gaozu's earlier rescue, he had him transferred to his own command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.

sentences.zh: 應順初，晉高祖鎮常山，唐明宗召赴闕，會閔帝出奔，與晉高祖相遇於途，遂俱入衛州，泊於郵舍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun, the Jin Emperor Gaozu was stationed at Changshan when Emperor Mingzong of Tang summoned him to court. It happened that Emperor Min was fleeing, and he met the Jin Emperor Gaozu on the road; they then both entered Weizhou and lodged at a postal station.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingshun, while the Jin emperor held Changshan, Mingzong summoned him to court. Emperor Min was then in flight, and the two met on the road, entered Weizhou together, and lodged at a postal station.

sentences.zh: 閔帝左右謀害晉高祖，帝密遣禦士石敢袖鎚立於晉高祖後，及有變，敢擁晉高祖入一室，以巨木塞門，敢尋死焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Min's attendants plotted to kill the Jin Emperor Gaozu. The Emperor secretly sent the guard Shi Gan, with a hammer hidden in his sleeve, to stand behind the Jin Emperor Gaozu. When trouble arose, Gan shielded the Jin Emperor Gaozu into a room and blocked the door with a great beam of timber; Gan soon died in the act.
translations.idiomatic: Men close to Emperor Min plotted to kill the Jin emperor. Gaozu secretly posted his guardsman Shi Gan, hammer concealed in his sleeve, behind him. When the attack came, Gan hustled the Jin emperor into a room and barred the door with a heavy timber beam, and died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 帝率眾盡殺閔帝左右，遂免晉高祖於難。

translations.literal: The Emperor led his men and killed all of Emperor Min's attendants, thereby saving the Jin Emperor Gaozu from peril.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then led his men and killed every one of Emperor Min's attendants, thus saving the Jin emperor from the plot.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》引《漢高祖實錄》云：是夜，偵知少帝伏甲，欲與從臣謀害晉高祖，詐屏人對語，方坐庭廡。

translations.literal: (Examination of Discrepancies in the Comprehensive Mirror, citing the Veritable Record of Han Gaozu, states: That night he learned that the young emperor had hidden armed men and intended, with his followers, to kill the Jin Emperor Gaozu; they feigned dismissal of attendants for private talk and were just then seated in the portico of the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror, Examination of Discrepancies, citing the Veritable Record of Han Gaozu: That night he learned the young emperor had hidden armed men and meant, with his followers, to murder the Jin emperor; they pretended to dismiss attendants for a private talk and were seated in the courtyard portico.

sentences.zh: 帝密遣禦士石敢袖鎚立於後，俄頃伏甲者起，敢有勇力，擁晉高祖入一室，以巨木塞門，敢力當其鋒，死之。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly sent the guard Shi Gan, with a hammer in his sleeve, to stand behind him. In a moment the hidden armed men rose. Gan was strong and brave; he shielded the Jin Emperor Gaozu into a room and blocked the door with a great timber. Gan met their assault with force and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu secretly posted Shi Gan behind him, hammer in his sleeve. Moments later the ambush rose. Gan was powerful; he pushed the Jin emperor into a room, barred the door with a heavy beam, met the rush head-on, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 帝解佩刀，遇夜晦，以在地葦炬未然者奮擊之，眾謂短兵也，遂散走。

translations.literal: The Emperor drew his belt dagger. The night was dark; he seized an unlit reed torch lying on the ground and struck out fiercely. The crowd thought it was a short weapon and scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drew his belt dagger. In the dark he snatched up an unlit reed torch from the ground and struck out wildly. The assailants took it for a drawn blade and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝乃匿身長垣下，聞帝親將李洪信謂人曰：「石太尉死矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor then hid himself beneath a long wall and heard the imperial intimate general Li Hongxin say to someone, "Commander Shi is dead.
translations.idiomatic: He hid beneath a long wall and heard the emperor's intimate general Li Hongxin tell someone, "Commander Shi is dead.

sentences.zh: 」帝隔垣呼洪信曰：「太尉無恙。

translations.literal: " The Emperor called across the wall to Hongxin, "The Commander is unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu called over the wall, "The commander is alive and well.

sentences.zh: 」乃逾垣出就洪信兵，共護晉高祖，殺建謀者，以少主授王宏贄。）〉

translations.literal: " He then climbed over the wall, joined Hongxin's troops, and together they protected the Jin Emperor Gaozu, killed those who had plotted the affair, and handed the young sovereign over to Wang Hongzan.)]
translations.idiomatic: " He climbed over the wall, joined Hongxin's troops, protected the Jin emperor, killed the plotters, and delivered the young sovereign to Wang Hongzan.)]

sentences.zh: 天福二年夏四月，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the second year of Tianfu, he was given the additional title of acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Tianfu 2, he received the additional title of acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 八月，改許州節度使，典軍如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to military commissioner of Xuzhou, with command of troops unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he became military commissioner of Xuzhou while retaining command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 三年夏四月，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the third year, he was given the additional title of acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, year 3, he was made acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，授侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he was appointed Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month he was appointed director-in-chief of the palace horse and foot guards.

sentences.zh: 十一月，移授宋州，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was transferred to Songzhou and given the additional title of acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was reassigned to Songzhou with the additional title of acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was given the additional title of Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was made concurrent grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時帝與杜重威同制加恩，帝憤然不樂，懇讓不受，杜門不出者數日。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor and Du Chongwei received favors by the same edict. The Emperor was angry and displeased, earnestly declined and would not accept, and shut his door and did not go out for several days.
translations.idiomatic: He and Du Chongwei had been honored by the same edict. Gaozu was openly displeased, repeatedly declined the honors, and stayed behind closed doors for days.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：知遠自以有佐命功，重威起於外戚，無大功，恥與之同制。

translations.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: Zhiyuan considered that he had merit in assisting the founding of the dynasty, while Chongwei had risen as an affinal kinsman without great achievement, and he was ashamed to share an edict with him.
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: Zhiyuan believed he had earned founding merit, whereas Chongwei had risen only as an imperial in-law without comparable service, and he was ashamed to be honored in the same edict.

sentences.zh: 制下數日，杜門四表辭不受。）〉

translations.literal: Several days after the edict was issued, he shut his door and sent memorials in all directions declining to accept.)]
translations.idiomatic: For days after the edict he kept his doors shut and memorialized from every quarter that he would not accept.)]

sentences.zh: 晉高祖怒，召宰相趙瑩等議落帝兵權，任歸私第。

translations.literal: The Jin Emperor Gaozu was angry and summoned the chief minister Zhao Ying and others to discuss stripping the Emperor of military authority and assigning him to private residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor was furious and summoned Chief Minister Zhao Ying and others to discuss stripping Gaozu of command and confining him to private life.

sentences.zh: 瑩等以為不可，乃遣端明殿學士和凝就第宣諭，帝乃承命。

translations.literal: Ying and the others held that this could not be done, so they sent the academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity He Ning to his residence to announce the imperial will, and the Emperor then accepted the order.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and his colleagues argued against it, so the court sent Academician He Ning of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity to his house with the imperial message, and Gaozu then accepted.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，改鄴都留守兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year he was made military governor of the Ye capital garrison, concurrently Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 5 he became garrison commander of the Ye capital while retaining direction of the palace horse and foot guards.

sentences.zh: 九月，奉詔赴闕，晉高祖幸其第。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, obeying an edict he went to court, and the Jin Emperor Gaozu visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he answered a summons to court, and the Jin emperor paid a visit to his residence.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，授北京留守、河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was appointed military governor of the Northern Capital garrison and military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 6 he was made garrison commander of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 7 he was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時天下大蝗，惟不入河東界。

translations.literal: At that time locusts ravaged the realm, but they did not enter the borders of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts plagued the empire, yet they never crossed into Hedong.

sentences.zh: 六月，晉高祖崩於鄴宮，少帝即位，加帝檢校太師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Jin Emperor Gaozu died at the Ye palace; the young emperor succeeded, and the Emperor was given the additional title of acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Jin emperor died at Ye; the young emperor succeeded, and Gaozu was made acting grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，進位中書令。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he was advanced to the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 8 he was promoted to director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開運元年正月，契丹南下，契丹主以大軍直抵澶州，遣蕃將偉王率兵入雁門。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun, the Khitan advanced south. The Khitan ruler led a great army straight to Chunzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei at the head of troops into Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaiyun 1 the Khitan marched south. Their ruler drove a great army straight to Chunzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei through Yanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以帝為幽州道行營招討使，帝大破偉王於忻口。

translations.literal: The court appointed the Emperor pacification commissioner of the Youzhou circuit campaign headquarters; he inflicted a great defeat on Prince Wei at Xinkou.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him pacification commissioner for the Youzhou campaign, and he routed Prince Wei at Xinkou.

sentences.zh: 尋奉詔起兵至土門，軍至樂平，會契丹退，乃還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, obeying an edict he raised troops and advanced to Tumen Pass; the army reached Leping, but when the Khitan withdrew he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon marched under edict as far as Tumen Pass and reached Leping, but turned back when the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，封太原王。

translations.literal: In the third month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 七月，兼北面行營都統。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was additionally made supreme commander of the northern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was also made supreme commander of the northern front.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，封北平王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 2 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，加守太尉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year he was given the additional title of Guardian Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 3 he was made guardian grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝誅吐渾白承福等五族凡四百人，以別部王義宗統其餘眾。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor executed the Tujue tribes of Bai Chengfu and four other clans, four hundred persons in all, and placed the remaining followers under the command of Wang Yizong of another division.
translations.idiomatic: That month he executed four hundred people of five Tujue clans led by Bai Chengfu and placed the survivors under Wang Yizong of another division.

sentences.zh: 九月，契丹犯塞，帝親率牙兵至朔州南陽武谷，大破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Khitan violated the frontier. The Emperor personally led his guard troops to Nanyangwu Valley south of Shuozhou and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, when the Khitan raided the frontier, he led his guard in person to Nanyangwu Valley south of Shuozhou and crushed them.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·郭進傳》：契丹屠安陽，高祖遣進拒戰，契丹敗走，以功除刺史。）〉

translations.literal: (Biography of Guo Jin in the Brief Account of the Eastern Capital states: the Khitan slaughtered Anyang; Gaozu sent Jin to resist; the Khitan were defeated and fled, and for his merit he was made prefect.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Brief Account of the Eastern Capital, Biography of Guo Jin: after the Khitan sacked Anyang, Gaozu sent Jin to meet them; the Khitan were routed, and he was made prefect for his service.)]

sentences.zh: 十一月，契丹主率蕃漢大軍由易、定抵鎮州，杜重威等駐軍於中渡橋以禦之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Khitan ruler led a great army of tribesmen and Han from Yi and Ding to Zhenzhou; Du Chongwei and others encamped at the Zhongdu Bridge to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Khitan ruler led a mixed tribal and Chinese army from Yi and Ding to Zhenzhou, while Du Chongwei and others held the Zhongdu Bridge against him.

sentences.zh: 十二月十日，杜重威等以全軍降於契丹。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the twelfth month Du Chongwei and others surrendered the entire army to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the twelfth month Du Chongwei surrendered his entire army to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 十七日，相州節度使張彥澤受契丹命，陷京城，遷少帝於開封府。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day Zhang Yanze, military commissioner of Xiangzhou, acting on Khitan orders, seized the capital and moved the young emperor to Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth Zhang Yanze of Xiangzhou, acting on Khitan orders, took the capital and removed the young emperor to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之大駭，分兵守境，以備寇患。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this he was greatly alarmed and divided his troops to guard the borders against invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was deeply alarmed and posted troops along his borders to guard against attack.

sentences.zh: 天福十二年春正月丁亥朔，契丹主入東京。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of spring in the twelfth year of Tianfu, the cyclical day dinghai, the Khitan ruler entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the new year's day dinghai of the first spring month, Tianfu 12, the Khitan ruler entered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，晉少帝蒙塵於封禪寺。

translations.literal: On guisi the young emperor of Jin suffered disgrace at the Fengchan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the young Jin emperor was held captive at Fengchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，少帝北遷。

translations.literal: On guimao the young emperor was moved north.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the young emperor was sent north.

sentences.zh: 二月丁巳朔，契丹主具漢法服，禦崇元殿受朝，制改晉國為大遼國，大赦天下，號會同十年。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, the cyclical day dingsi, the Khitan ruler put on Chinese court dress, took the throne in the Hall of Veneration of the Origin to receive homage, and by edict changed the state of Jin to the Great Liao state, proclaimed a general amnesty, and styled the era the tenth year of Huitong.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon dingsi in the second month the Khitan ruler donned Chinese court robes, held court in the Hall of Veneration of the Origin, changed Jin to Great Liao by edict, proclaimed a general amnesty, and dated the reign the tenth year of Huitong.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝遣牙將王峻奉表於契丹，契丹主賜詔褒美，呼帝為兒，又賜木拐一。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor sent his guard officer Wang Jun to present a memorial to the Khitan. The Khitan ruler granted an edict of praise, called the Emperor "son," and also bestowed one wooden staff.
translations.idiomatic: That month Gaozu sent his guard officer Wang Jun with a memorial to the Khitan court. The Khitan ruler replied with a commendatory edict, addressed him as "son," and gave him a wooden staff.

sentences.zh: 蕃法，貴重大臣方得此賜，亦猶漢儀賜几杖之比也。

translations.literal: By tribal law only honored great ministers received this gift; it was comparable to the Han ritual of bestowing armrests and staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Khitan custom only the most honored ministers received such a gift, comparable to the Han court's bestowal of armrests and staffs.

sentences.zh: 王峻持持而歸，契丹望之皆避路。

translations.literal: Wang Jun carried it back, and when the Khitan saw it they all gave way on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun carried it home, and Khitan onlookers cleared the road before him.

sentences.zh: 及峻至太原，帝知契丹政亂，乃議建號焉。

translations.literal: When Jun reached Taiyuan, the Emperor knew that Khitan government was in disorder and thereupon deliberated on establishing a dynastic title.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached Taiyuan, Gaozu saw that Khitan rule was falling into disorder and began to plan proclaiming a new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 是月，秦州節度使何建以其地入於蜀。

translations.literal: That month He Jian, military commissioner of Qinzhou, surrendered his territory to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: That month He Jian of Qinzhou surrendered his territory to Shu.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，河東行軍司馬張彥威與文武將吏等，以中原無主，帝威望日隆，群情所屬，上箋勸進，帝謙讓不允。

translations.literal: On wuchen Zhang Yanwei, campaigning marshal of Hedong, together with civil and military officers, because the Central Plains lacked a ruler and the Emperor's prestige daily rose and all hearts turned to him, submitted a memorial urging accession; the Emperor modestly declined and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Zhang Yanwei, Hedong campaigning marshal, with civil and military officers, urged him to take the throne because the Central Plains had no ruler and all eyes were turning to his rising prestige. Gaozu declined.

sentences.zh: 自是群官三上箋，諸軍將吏、緇黃耆耋，相次迫請，教答允之。

translations.literal: From then on the officials submitted memorials three times; military officers, monks and priests, and elders pressed him in succession, and by edict he answered that he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials memorialized three times; officers, clergy, and elders pressed him in turn until he assented by edict.

sentences.zh: 庚午，陜府屯駐奉國指揮使趙暉、侯章、都頭王晏殺契丹監軍及副使劉願，暉自稱留後。

translations.literal: On gengwu Zhao Hui, commander of the Fengguo Army stationed at Shaan prefecture, Hou Zhang, and company chief Wang Yan killed the Khitan military supervisor and vice commissioner Liu Yuan; Hui styled himself acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Zhao Hui of the Fengguo Army at Shaan, Hou Zhang, and company chief Wang Yan killed the Khitan supervisor Liu Yuan and his deputy; Hui declared himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 契丹因授暉陜州兵馬留後，侯章為本州馬步軍都指揮使，王晏為副都指揮使，暉等不受命。

translations.literal: The Khitan thereupon appointed Hui military commissioner of Shaanzhou, Zhang director of the prefecture's horse and foot forces, and Yan vice director, but Hui and the others did not accept the orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then appointed Hui military commissioner of Shaan, Zhang director of local horse and foot forces, and Yan his deputy, but they refused.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·王晏傳》：開運末，與本軍都校趙暉、忠衛都校侯章等戍陜州。

translations.literal: (Biography of Wang Yan in the History of Song states: at the end of Kaiyun he garrisoned Shaanzhou together with the army commander Zhao Hui of his unit and the Zhongwei commander Hou Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: (History of Song, Biography of Wang Yan: at the end of Kaiyun he was posted to Shaan with his unit commander Zhao Hui and Zhongwei commander Hou Zhang.

sentences.zh: 會契丹至汴，遣其將劉願據陜，恣行暴虐。

translations.literal: When the Khitan reached Bian they sent their general Liu Yuan to hold Shaan and indulged in violent oppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan reached Bian they sent Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, where he ruled with savage cruelty.

sentences.zh: 晏與暉等謀曰：「今契丹南侵，天下洶洶，英雄豪傑固當乘時自奮。

translations.literal: Yan plotted with Hui and the others, saying, "Now the Khitan invade south and the realm is in turmoil; heroes and men of mark ought surely to seize the moment and rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said to Hui and the others, "The Khitan are invading south and the realm is in uproar. Men of spirit ought to seize the moment.

sentences.zh: 且聞太原劉公，威德遠被，人心歸服，若殺願送款河東，為天下倡首，則取富貴如反掌耳！

translations.literal: Moreover we hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's authority and virtue reach far and men's hearts submit to him. If we kill Yuan and send allegiance to Hedong, taking the lead for the realm, then gaining wealth and rank will be like turning the hand!
translations.idiomatic: We hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's prestige reaches far and men gladly follow him. Kill Yuan, submit to Hedong, and lead the realm—and wealth and rank will come as easily as turning one's hand!

sentences.zh: 」暉等然之。

translations.literal: " Hui and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 晏乃率敢死士數人，夜逾城入府署，劫庫兵給其徒。

translations.literal: Yan then led several dare-to-die men, climbed over the wall by night into the government compound, and seized weapons from the arsenal to arm his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yan led a handful of dare-to-die men over the wall by night into the government compound and seized arms from the arsenal for his men.

sentences.zh: 遲明，斬願首懸府門外。

translations.literal: At daybreak he beheaded Yuan and hung his head outside the government gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he beheaded Yuan and displayed his head outside the government gate.

sentences.zh: 眾請暉為帥，章為本城副指揮使、內外巡檢使兼都虞候，乃遣其子漢倫奉表晉陽。）〉

translations.literal: The crowd asked Hui to be commander, Zhang to be deputy commander of the prefecture, interior and exterior patrol commissioner, and chief military judge, and they then sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.)]
translations.idiomatic: The troops made Hui commander, Zhang deputy commander and patrol commissioner, and sent his son Hanlun with a memorial to Jinyang.)]

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝於太原宮受冊，即皇帝位，制改晉開運四年為天福十二年。

translations.literal: On xinwei the Emperor received the investiture at the Taiyuan palace, ascended the imperial throne, and by edict changed the fourth year of Jin Kaiyun to the twelfth year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he was invested at the Taiyuan palace and took the throne, changing Jin's Kaiyun 4 to Tianfu 12 by edict.

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》云：漢祖仍稱天福年號，曰：「予未忍忘晉也。」）〉

translations.literal: (Records of the Khitan State states: Han Gaozu still used the Tianfu reign title, saying, "I cannot yet bear to forget Jin.")]
translations.idiomatic: (Records of the Khitan State: Han Gaozu kept the Tianfu reign title, saying, "I am not yet ready to forget Jin.")]

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝以晉帝舉族北遷，憤惋久之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, because the Jin emperor and his entire clan were moved north, the Emperor was angry and grieved for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, learning that the Jin emperor and his whole clan had been sent north, Gaozu brooded in anger and grief for a long time.

sentences.zh: 是日，率親兵趨土門路，邀迎晉帝至壽陽，聞其已過，乃還。

translations.literal: That day he led his personal troops toward the Tumen route to intercept and welcome the Jin emperor as far as Shouyang; hearing that he had already passed, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he led his personal guard toward Tumen Pass to intercept the Jin emperor and welcome him as far as Shouyang, but turned back on hearing he had already passed.

sentences.zh: 契丹聞帝建號，偽制削奪帝官爵。

translations.literal: When the Khitan heard that the Emperor had established a dynastic title, by a spurious edict they stripped him of rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan learned he had proclaimed a dynasty, they issued a counterfeit edict stripping him of rank and titles.

sentences.zh: 以通事耿崇美為潞州節度使，高唐英為相州節度使，崔廷勛為河陽節度使，以扼要害之地。

translations.literal: They appointed the interpreter Geng Chongmei military commissioner of Luzhou, Gao Tangying of Xiangzhou, and Cui Tingxun of Heyang, in order to choke the strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: They installed the interpreter Geng Chongmei at Luzhou, Gao Tangying at Xiangzhou, and Cui Tingxun at Heyang to hold the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，磁州賊帥梁暉據相州。

translations.literal: On dingchou the bandit chief Liang Hui of Cizhou seized Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Cizhou rebel Liang Hui seized Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝遣都將史宏肇率兵討代州，平之。

translations.literal: On jimao the Emperor sent the commander Shi Hongzhao at the head of troops to attack Daizhou and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he sent Commander Shi Hongzhao against Daizhou and pacified it.

sentences.zh: 初，代州刺史王暉叛歸契丹，宏肇一鼓而拔之，斬暉以徇。

translations.literal: Earlier the prefect of Daizhou Wang Hui had defected to the Khitan; Hongzhao took the city at the first assault and beheaded Hui as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Daizhou prefect Wang Hui had earlier defected to the Khitan; Hongzhao stormed the city at the first blow and executed Hui as a warning.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，權晉州兵馬留後張晏洪奏，軍亂，殺知州副使駱從朗及括錢使、諫議大夫趙熙，以城歸順。

translations.literal: On gengchen the acting military commissioner of Jinzhou Zhang Yanhong memorialized that the army had mutinied, killed the vice prefect Luo Conglang and the tax-collection commissioner, Remonstrance Grandee Zhao Xi, and submitted the city in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen acting Jinzhou commissioner Zhang Yanhong reported that the garrison had mutinied, killed vice prefect Luo Conglang, tax commissioner Remonstrance Grandee Zhao Xi, and submitted the city.

sentences.zh: 時晉州留後劉在明赴東京，朝於契丹，從朗知軍州事，帝方遣使張晏洪、辛處明等告諭登極，從朗囚之本城。

translations.literal: At that time the Jinzhou acting commissioner Liu Zaiming had gone to the Eastern Capital to attend court with the Khitan; Conglang was administering military and prefectural affairs. The Emperor had just sent Zhang Yanhong, Xin Chuming, and others to announce his accession, and Conglang imprisoned them in the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou acting commissioner Liu Zaiming was then at the Eastern Capital paying court to the Khitan, while Conglang ran local affairs. Gaozu had just sent Zhang Yanhong and Xin Chuming to announce his accession, and Conglang imprisoned them in the city.

sentences.zh: 大將藥可儔殺從朗於理所，州民相率害趙熙，三軍請晏洪為留後，處明為都監。

translations.literal: The great general Yao Keyou killed Conglang at the government office; the people of the prefecture together killed Zhao Xi; the three armies asked Yanhong to be acting commissioner and Chuming chief supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: General Yao Keyou killed Conglang in the government hall; townspeople together killed Zhao Xi; the armies asked for Yanhong as acting commissioner and Chuming as chief supervisor.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，權陜州留後趙暉、權潞州留後王守恩，並上表歸順。

translations.literal: On xinsi the acting commissioners Zhao Hui of Shaanzhou and Wang Shouen of Luzhou both submitted memorials of allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi acting commissioners Zhao Hui of Shaan and Wang Shouen of Lu both submitted memorials of submission.

sentences.zh: 癸未，澶州賊帥王瓊與其眾斷本州浮橋，瓊敗，死之。

translations.literal: On guiwei the bandit chief Wang Qiong of Chunzhou and his followers cut the prefecture's pontoon bridge; Qiong was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the Chunzhou rebel Wang Qiong and his men cut the prefecture's pontoon bridge; Qiong was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 時契丹以族人朗鄂為澶州節度使，朗鄂性貪虐，吏民苦之。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan appointed their clansman Lange as military commissioner of Chunzhou; Lange was greedy and cruel by nature, and officials and people suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had appointed their kinsman Lange military commissioner of Chunzhou; greedy and brutal by nature, he made life miserable for officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 瓊為水運什長，乃構夏津賊帥張乙，得千餘人，沿河而上，中夜竊發，自南城殺守將，絕浮航，入北城，朗悟據牙城以拒之。

translations.literal: Qiong was a squad chief of water transport; he then joined with the bandit chief Zhang Yi of Xiajin and gathered more than a thousand men. They went upriver, stole a march at midnight, killed the defending general from the south city, cut the pontoon crossing, and entered the north city; Langwu held the headquarters compound to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong, a water-transport squad chief, allied with the Xiajin bandit Zhang Yi and raised more than a thousand men. They moved upriver, struck at midnight from the south city, killed the garrison commander, severed the pontoon bridge, and entered the north city, while Langwu barricaded himself in the headquarters compound.

sentences.zh: 數日，會契丹救至，瓊敗死焉。

translations.literal: Several days later Khitan relief arrived; Qiong was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Khitan reinforcements arrived; Qiong was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 契丹主初聞其變也，懼甚，由是大河之南無久留之意，尋遣天雄軍節度使杜重威歸鎮。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler first heard of this disturbance he was greatly afraid; from this he had no intention of remaining long south of the Great River, and soon sent Du Chongwei, military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army, back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler first heard of the uprising he was deeply alarmed and no longer wished to linger south of the Yellow River; he soon sent Tianxiong commissioner Du Chongwei back to his command.

sentences.zh: 三月丙戌朔，詔河東管內，自前稅外，雜色征配一切除放。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, the cyclical day bingxu, an edict proclaimed that within the Hedong circuit, aside from previous taxes, all miscellaneous levies and assignments were entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon bingxu in the third month an edict remitted every miscellaneous levy in the Hedong circuit beyond standing taxes.

sentences.zh: 是日，契丹主坐崇元殿行入閣之禮，契丹主以舅蕭翰為宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: That day the Khitan ruler sat in the Hall of Veneration of the Origin and performed the ceremony of entering the inner court; the Khitan ruler appointed his maternal uncle Xiao Han military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Khitan ruler held court in the Hall of Veneration of the Origin and performed the inner-court ceremony; he also appointed his uncle Xiao Han military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，權延州留後高允權遣判官李彬奏：本道節度使周密為三軍所逐，以允權知留後事，上表歸順。

translations.literal: On xinmao the acting Yanzhou commissioner Gao Yunquan sent his aide Li Bin to memorialize: the circuit military commissioner Zhou Mi had been driven out by the three armies; Yunquan was administering as acting commissioner and submitted a memorial of allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao acting Yanzhou commissioner Gao Yunquan reported through aide Li Bin that the circuit commissioner Zhou Mi had been expelled by the armies, that Yunquan was acting in his place, and that they submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝召密赴行在。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor summoned Mi to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor summoned Zhou Mi to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，丹州都指揮使高彥珣殺偽命刺史，據城歸命。

translations.literal: On renchen the director of Danzhou Gao Yancong killed the spuriously appointed prefect, held the city, and submitted to command.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Danzhou director Gao Yancong killed the Khitan-appointed prefect, held the city, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，契丹主發自東京還本國。

translations.literal: On renyin the Khitan ruler set out from the Eastern Capital to return to his own state.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Khitan ruler left the Eastern Capital for home.

sentences.zh: 是日，宿於赤崗，至晡，有大聲如雷，起於敵帳之下。

translations.literal: That day he lodged at Chigang; toward the hour of shen there was a great sound like thunder rising beneath the enemy encampment.
translations.idiomatic: That day he camped at Chigang; toward evening a thunderous roar rose from beneath the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 契丹自黎陽濟河，遂趨相州。

translations.literal: The Khitan crossed the river from Liyang and then pressed toward Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan crossed the river at Liyang and marched on Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，帝以北京馬步軍都指揮使、泗州防禦使、檢校太保劉崇為太原尹、檢校太尉，以北京馬步軍都虞候郭從義為鄭州防禦使、檢校太保，以北京興捷左廂都指揮使李洪信為陳州刺史、檢校司徒，以興捷右廂都指揮使尚洪遷為單州刺史、檢校司徒，以北京武節左廂都指揮使蓋萬為蔡州刺史，以武節右廂都指揮使周暉為濮州刺史，以保寧都指揮使朱奉千為隨州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengxu the Emperor appointed Liu Chong, Director-in-Chief of the Beijing Horse and Foot Forces and defense commissioner of Sizhou with acting Grand Guardian, as prefect of Taiyuan and acting Grand Marshal; Guo Congyi, chief military judge of the Beijing Horse and Foot Forces, as defense commissioner of Zhengzhou and acting Grand Guardian; Li Hongxin, commander of the left wing of the Beijing Xingjie Army, as prefect of Chenzhou and acting Minister of Works; Shang Hongqian, commander of the right wing of the Xingjie Army, as prefect of Shanzhou and acting Minister of Works; Gai Wan, commander of the left wing of the Beijing Wujie Army, as prefect of Caizhou; Zhou Hui, commander of the right wing of the Wujie Army, as prefect of Puzhou; and Zhu Fengqian, commander of the Baoning Army, as prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor made Liu Chong, Beijing horse-and-foot commander and Sizhou defense commissioner, prefect of Taiyuan with acting grand marshal; Guo Congyi Beijing chief military judge, Zhengzhou defense commissioner and acting grand guardian; Li Hongxin of the Beijing Xingjie left wing, Chenzhou prefect and acting minister of works; Shang Hongqian of the Xingjie right wing, Shanzhou prefect and acting minister of works; Gai Wan of the Wujie left wing, Caizhou prefect; Zhou Hui of the Wujie right wing, Puzhou prefect; and Zhu Fengqian of the Baoning Army, Suizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，吐渾節度使王義宗加檢校太尉，以前忻州刺史秦習為耀州團練使。

translations.literal: On xinhai the Tujue military commissioner Wang Yizong was given the additional title of acting Grand Marshal, and the former prefect of Xinzhou Qin Xi was made regimental commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Tujue commissioner Wang Yizong was made acting grand marshal, and former Xinzhou prefect Qin Xi became regimental commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以北京副留守、檢校司徒白文珂為河中節度使、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: On guichou Bai Wenke, deputy military governor of the Beijing garrison and acting Minister of Works, was made military commissioner of Hezhong and acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Beijing deputy garrison commander Bai Wenke was made Hezhong military commissioner and acting grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己未，以北京馬軍都指揮使、集州刺史劉信為滑州節度使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使、檢校太傅；

translations.literal: In summer, on jiwei of the fourth month, Liu Xin, Director of the Beijing Horse Forces and prefect of Jizhou, was made military commissioner of Huazhou, Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse Guards, and acting Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month, on jiwei, Beijing horse commander and Jizhou prefect Liu Xin became Huazhou military commissioner, palace horse commander, and acting grand tutor;

sentences.zh: 以北京隨使、右都押衙楊邠為權樞密使、檢校太保；

translations.literal: Yang Bin, Beijing attendant and right chief escort officer, was made acting Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Beijing attendant Yang Bin became acting commissioner of military affairs and acting grand guardian;

sentences.zh: 以北京武節都指揮使、雷州刺史宏肇為許州節度使，充待衛步軍都指揮使、檢校太傅；

translations.literal: Hongzhao, commander of the Beijing Wujie Army and prefect of Leizhou, was made military commissioner of Xuzhou, Director-in-Chief of the Palace Foot Guards, and acting Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Beijing Wujie commander and Leizhou prefect Hongzhao became Xuzhou military commissioner, palace foot commander, and acting grand tutor;

sentences.zh: 以北京牢城都指揮使、壁州刺史常思為鄧州節度使、檢校太傅兼權北京馬步軍都指揮使、三城巡檢使；

translations.literal: Chang Si, commander of the Beijing Laocheng Army and prefect of Bizhou, was made military commissioner of Dengzhou, acting Grand Tutor, concurrently acting Director-in-Chief of the Beijing Horse and Foot Forces, and inspector of the Three Cities;
translations.idiomatic: Beijing Laocheng commander and Bizhou prefect Chang Si became Dengzhou military commissioner and acting grand tutor, concurrently acting Beijing horse-and-foot commander and inspector of the Three Cities;

sentences.zh: 以河東行軍司馬張彥威為同州節度使、檢校太保；

translations.literal: Zhang Yanwei, campaigning marshal of Hedong, was made military commissioner of Tongzhou and acting Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Hedong campaigning marshal Zhang Yanwei became Tongzhou military commissioner and acting grand guardian;

sentences.zh: 以蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威為權樞密使、檢校司徒；

translations.literal: Guo Wei, chief clerk of tribal and Chinese horse and foot forces, was made acting Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei, chief clerk of the mixed tribal and Chinese forces, became acting commissioner of military affairs and acting minister of works;

sentences.zh: 以河東左都押衙扈彥珂為宣徽南院使、檢校司徒；

translations.literal: Hu Yanke, left chief escort officer of Hedong, was made commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and acting Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: Hedong left chief escort Hu Yanke became commissioner of the southern palace secretariat bureau and acting minister of works;

sentences.zh: 以右都押衙王浩為宣徽北院使、檢校司徒；

translations.literal: Wang Hao, right chief escort officer, was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and acting Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: Right chief escort Wang Hao became commissioner of the northern palace secretariat bureau and acting minister of works;

sentences.zh: 以兩使都孔目官王章為權三司使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang, chief clerk of the two bureaus, was made acting Commissioner of the Three Departments and acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang, chief clerk of the two bureaus, became acting commissioner of the three departments and acting grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 是日，契丹主取相州，殺留後梁暉。

translations.literal: That day the Khitan ruler took Xiangzhou and killed the acting commissioner Liang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Khitan ruler took Xiangzhou and killed acting commissioner Liang Hui.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李穀傳》：潛遣河朔酋豪暉入據安陽，契丹主患之，即謀北旋，會有告契丹以城中虛弱者，契丹還攻安陽，陷其城。）〉

translations.literal: (Biography of Li Gu in the History of Song states: he secretly sent the Hebei chieftain Hui to seize and hold Anyang. The Khitan ruler was troubled by this and at once planned to turn north; then someone reported to the Khitan that the city was weak, and the Khitan returned to attack Anyang and captured it.)]
translations.idiomatic: (History of Song, Biography of Li Gu: he secretly sent the Hebei chieftain Hui to hold Anyang. The Khitan ruler, alarmed, planned to withdraw north; when someone reported the city was weak, he turned back, attacked Anyang, and captured it.)]

sentences.zh: 暉，磁州滏陽人，少為盜，會契丹入汴，暉收集徒黨，先入磁州，無所侵犯，遣使送款於帝。

translations.literal: Hui was a native of Fuyang in Cizhou and in youth was a bandit. When the Khitan entered Bian, Hui gathered his followers, first entered Cizhou without committing violations, and sent envoys to offer allegiance to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, a native of Fuyang in Cizhou, had been a bandit in his youth. When the Khitan entered Bian he gathered followers, took Cizhou without looting it, and sent envoys offering allegiance to the throne.

sentences.zh: 暉偵知相州頗積兵仗，且無守備，遂以三月二十一日夜與其徒逾垣而入，殺契丹數十人，奪器甲數萬計，遂據其城。

translations.literal: Hui learned by reconnaissance that Xiangzhou had stored considerable arms yet lacked defenses; on the night of the twenty-first day of the third month he and his followers climbed over the wall and entered, killed several tens of Khitan, seized arms and armor numbering in the tens of thousands, and thereupon held the city.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Xiangzhou held large stores of weapons but few defenders, he and his men scaled the walls on the night of the twenty-first of the third month, killed dozens of Khitan, seized tens of thousands of arms and armor, and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 契丹主先遣偽命相州節度使高唐英率兵討之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler first sent the spuriously appointed military commissioner of Xiangzhou Gao Tangying at the head of troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler first sent the Khitan-appointed Xiangzhou commissioner Gao Tangying against him with an army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，契丹主至城下，是月四日攻拔之，遂屠其城。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan ruler reached the foot of the city; on the fourth day of that month he stormed and took it, then slaughtered the entire city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan ruler arrived beneath the walls; on the fourth of that month he stormed the city and then massacred its people.

sentences.zh: 翌日，契丹主北去，命高唐英鎮之，唐英閱城中遺民，得男女七百人而已。

translations.literal: The next day the Khitan ruler went north and ordered Gao Tangying to garrison it. Tangying reviewed the survivors in the city and found only seven hundred men and women.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Khitan ruler marched north and left Gao Tangying to garrison the ruins; Tangying found only seven hundred survivors, men and women together.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，王繼宏鎮相州，奏於城中得髑髏十餘萬，殺人之數，從可知也。

translations.literal: During Qianyou, when Wang Jihong was stationed at Xiangzhou, he memorialized that more than a hundred thousand skulls were found in the city; the number of those killed can thus be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou, when Wang Jihong governed Xiangzhou, he reported finding more than a hundred thousand skulls in the city—a measure of the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以石州刺史易全章為洺州團練使，以前遼州刺史安真為宿州團練使，以嵐州刺史孟行超為潁州團練使，以汾州刺史武彥宏為曹州防禦使，以前憲州刺史慕容信為齊州防禦使，以遼州刺史薛瓊為亳州防禦使，以沁州刺史李漢韜為汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: On gengshen Yi Quanzhang, prefect of Shizhou, was made regimental commissioner of Mingzhou; An Zhen, former prefect of Liaozhou, regimental commissioner of Suzhou; Meng Xingchao, prefect of Lanzhou, regimental commissioner of Yingzhou; Wu Yanhong, prefect of Fenzhou, defense commissioner of Caozhou; Murong Xin, former prefect of Xianzhou, defense commissioner of Qizhou; Xue Qiong, prefect of Liaozhou, defense commissioner of Bozhou; and Li Hantao, prefect of Qinzhou, defense commissioner of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the emperor appointed Yi Quanzhang of Shizhou regimental commissioner of Mingzhou; former Liaozhou prefect An Zhen, Suzhou; Lanzhou prefect Meng Xingchao, Yingzhou; Fenzhou prefect Wu Yanhong, Caozhou; former Xianzhou prefect Murong Xin, Qizhou; Liaozhou prefect Xue Qiong, Bozhou; and Qinzhou prefect Li Hantao, Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，冊魏國夫人李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On guihai Lady Li, Madame of the State of Wei, was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Lady Li of Wei was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以皇長子承訓為左衛上將軍，第二子承祐為左衛大將軍，第三子承勛為右衛大將軍，皇女彭城郡君宋氏封永寧公主，皇侄承赟為右衛上將軍。

translations.literal: On jiazi the eldest imperial son Chengxun (承訓) was made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard; the second son Chengyou, Great General of the Left Guard; the third son Chengxun (承勛), Great General of the Right Guard; the imperial daughter, Lady Song of Pengcheng commandery, was enfeoffed as Princess Yongning; and the imperial nephew Chengyun was made General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the eldest son Chengxun became general-in-chief of the Left Guard; the second son Chengyou, great general of the Left Guard; the third son Chengxun, great general of the Right Guard; the emperor's daughter, Lady Song of Pengcheng, was enfeoffed as Princess Yongning; and his nephew Chengyun became general-in-chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 以河東節度判官蘇逢吉為中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿大學士，以河東觀察判官蘇禹珪為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Su Fengji, adjutant of the Hedong military commission, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; Su Yugui, adjutant of the Hedong observation commission, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong commission adjutant Su Fengji became vice director of the Secretariat, concurrent grand councilor, and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; Hedong observation adjutant Su Yugui became vice director and concurrent grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 升府州為節鎮，加永安軍額。

translations.literal: Fuzhou was elevated to a military commission and given the designation Yong'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou was elevated to a full military commission under the designation Yong'an Army.

sentences.zh: 以振武節度使、府州團練使折從阮為永安軍節度使，行府州刺史、檢校太尉；

translations.literal: Zhe Congruan, military commissioner of Zhenwu and regimental commissioner of Fuzhou, was made military commissioner of the Yong'an Army, acting prefect of Fuzhou, and acting Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Zhenwu commissioner and Fuzhou regimental commissioner Zhe Congruan became Yong'an military commissioner, acting Fuzhou prefect, and acting grand marshal;

sentences.zh: 以北京隨使、左都押衙劉銖為河陽節度使；

translations.literal: Liu Zhu, Beijing attendant and left chief escort officer, was made military commissioner of Heyang;
translations.idiomatic: Beijing attendant and left chief escort Liu Zhu became Heyang military commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以河東支使韓祚為左諫議大夫，充樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Han Zuo, branch commissioner of Hedong, was made Left Remonstrance Grandee and Academician Direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong branch commissioner Han Zuo became left remonstrance grandee and direct academician of the bureau of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，遣史宏肇率兵一萬人趨潞州。

translations.literal: On yichou Shi Hongzhao was sent at the head of ten thousand troops toward Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Shi Hongzhao marched toward Luzhou with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以權知潞州軍州事、左驍衛大將軍王守恩為潞州節度使、檢校太保；

translations.literal: On bingyin Wang Shouen, acting administrator of Luzhou military and prefectural affairs and Great General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, was made military commissioner of Luzhou and acting Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin acting Luzhou administrator and left valiant-cavalry great general Wang Shouen became Luzhou military commissioner and acting grand guardian;

sentences.zh: 以權點檢延州軍州事高允權為延州節度使、檢校太保；

translations.literal: Gao Yunquan, acting inspector of Yanzhou military and prefectural affairs, was made military commissioner of Yanzhou and acting Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Acting Yanzhou inspector Gao Yunquan became Yanzhou military commissioner and acting grand guardian;

sentences.zh: 以岢嵐軍使鄭謙為忻州刺史，遙領應州節度使，充忻、代二州義軍都部署。

translations.literal: Zheng Qian, commander of the Kelan Army, was made prefect of Xinzhou, held the military commission of Yingzhou in absentia, and served as supreme commander of the loyal armies of Xin and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Kelan Army commander Zheng Qian became Xinzhou prefect, held Yingzhou in absentia, and commanded the loyal armies of Xin and Dai.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以河東都巡館驛、沿河巡檢使閻萬進為嵐州刺史，領朔州節度使，充嵐、憲二州義軍都制置。

translations.literal: On dingmao Yan Wanjin, Hedong inspector of post stations and river patrol commissioner, was made prefect of Lanzhou, held the military commission of Shuozhou, and served as supreme controller of the loyal armies of Lan and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Hedong post-station inspector and river patrol commissioner Yan Wanjin became Lanzhou prefect, held Shuozhou, and commanded the loyal armies of Lan and Xian.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，權河陽留後武行德以城來歸。

translations.literal: On wuchen the acting Heyang commissioner Wu Xingde submitted the city in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen acting Heyang commissioner Wu Xingde submitted his city.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主將發東京，船載武庫兵仗，自汴浮河，欲置之於北地，遣奉國都虞候武行德部送，與軍士千餘人並家屬俱行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Khitan ruler was about to depart the Eastern Capital, he loaded the arsenal arms on boats and floated them downriver from Bian, intending to place them in the northern lands. He sent Wu Xingde, chief military judge of the Fengguo Army, to escort them, together with more than a thousand soldiers and their families.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the Khitan ruler prepared to leave the Eastern Capital, he loaded arsenal weapons onto boats at Bian to float north and sent Fengguo chief military judge Wu Xingde to escort them with more than a thousand soldiers and their families.

sentences.zh: 至河陰，軍亂，奪兵仗，殺契丹監吏，眾推行德為帥，與河陰屯駐軍士合，乃自汜水抵河陽。

translations.literal: At Heyin the army mutinied, seized the weapons, killed the Khitan supervising officials, and the crowd made Xingde commander. Joining with the garrison troops stationed at Heyin, they then went from Sishui to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin the escort mutinied, seized the weapons, killed the Khitan supervisors, and made Xingde their commander. Joining the Heyin garrison, they marched from Sishui to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 河陽偽命節度使崔廷勛率兵拒之，兵敗，行德等追躡之，廷勛棄城而遁，行德因據其城。

translations.literal: Cui Tingxun, the spuriously appointed military commissioner of Heyang, led troops to resist them but was defeated. Xingde and the others pursued him; Tingxun abandoned the city and fled, and Xingde thereupon held it.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan-appointed Heyang commissioner Cui Tingxun marched out to resist but was routed; Xingde pursued him, Tingxun fled, and Xingde seized the city.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略武行德傳》：行德陷於契丹，偽請自效，因遣送將校數十人護所取尚方鎧甲還北方。

translations.literal: (Biography of Wu Xingde in the Brief Account of the Eastern Capital states: Xingde had fallen into Khitan hands and falsely offered to serve them; they therefore sent him with several tens of officers and men to escort the imperial armor they had taken back to the north.
translations.idiomatic: (Brief Account of the Eastern Capital, Biography of Wu Xingde: captured by the Khitan, he pretended to serve them and was sent north with several dozen officers to escort seized imperial armor.

sentences.zh: 至河陰，行德謂眾曰：「我與若等能為邊地鬼耶？

translations.literal: At Heyin Xingde said to the crowd, "Are you and I to become ghosts on the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin he told the men, "Are we to become ghosts on the frontier?

sentences.zh: 」眾素伏其威名，皆曰：「惟命。

translations.literal: " The crowd had long submitted to his martial renown and all said, "We obey your command.
translations.idiomatic: " They had long respected his reputation and answered, "We follow your lead.

sentences.zh: 」遂攻孟州，走其節度使崔廷勛，悉以府庫分諸校，而權領州事。

translations.literal: " They then attacked Mengzhou, drove out its military commissioner Cui Tingxun, divided the treasury among the officers, and Xingde acted as administrator of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " They attacked Mengzhou, drove out commissioner Cui Tingxun, divided the treasury among the officers, and Xingde acted as prefect.

sentences.zh: 遣其弟行友詣太原勸進。）〉

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother Xingyou to Taiyuan to urge accession.)]
translations.idiomatic: He sent his brother Xingyou to Taiyuan to urge the throne.)]

sentences.zh: 偽命西京留守劉晞棄洛城，南走許州，遂奔東京，洛京巡檢使方太自署知留守事。

translations.literal: Liu Xi, the spuriously appointed western capital military governor, abandoned Luoyang, fled south to Xuzhou, then ran to the Eastern Capital. Fang Tai, patrol commissioner of the Luo capital, styled himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan-appointed western capital governor Liu Xi abandoned Luoyang, fled south to Xuzhou, then to the Eastern Capital. Luoyang patrol commissioner Fang Tai declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太為武行德所害。

translations.literal: Before long Tai was killed by Wu Xingde.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fang Tai was killed by Wu Xingde.

sentences.zh: 是日，蕃將耿崇美屯澤州，史宏肇遣先鋒將馬誨率兵擊之，崇美退保懷州。

translations.literal: That day the tribal general Geng Chongmei encamped at Zezhou; Shi Hongzhao sent the vanguard commander Ma Hui at the head of troops to attack him, and Chongmei withdrew to defend Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That day tribal general Geng Chongmei held Zezhou; Shi Hongzhao sent vanguard Ma Hui against him, and Chongmei fell back to Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 崔廷勛以契丹眾攻武行德於河陽，行德出戰，為廷勛所敗。

translations.literal: Cui Tingxun attacked Wu Xingde at Heyang with Khitan forces; Xingde went out to battle and was defeated by Tingxun.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tingxun attacked Wu Xingde at Heyang with Khitan troops; Xingde marched out and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 汴州蕭翰遣蕃將高牟翰將兵援送劉晞復歸於洛。

translations.literal: Xiao Han of Bianzhou sent the tribal general Gao Mouhan with troops to escort Liu Xi back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Han of Bian sent tribal general Gao Mouhan with troops to escort Liu Xi back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 牟翰至，殺前澶州節度使潘環於洛陽。

translations.literal: When Mouhan arrived he killed the former military commissioner of Chunzhou Pan Huan at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Mouhan arrived he killed former Chunzhou commissioner Pan Huan at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以河陽都部署武行德為河陽節度使、檢校太尉，充一行馬步軍都部署。

translations.literal: On xinwei Wu Xingde, supreme commander of Heyang, was made military commissioner of Heyang and acting Grand Marshal, and served as supreme commander of the campaign horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Heyang supreme commander Wu Xingde became Heyang military commissioner and acting grand marshal, and supreme commander of the campaign forces.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，潞州節度使王守恩加檢校太尉，以前棣州刺史慕容彥超為澶州節度使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Wang Shouen, military commissioner of Luzhou, was given the additional title of acting Grand Marshal, and Murong Yanchao, former prefect of Dizhou, was made military commissioner of Chunzhou and acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Luzhou commissioner Wang Shouen was made acting grand marshal, and former Dizhou prefect Murong Yanchao became Chunzhou military commissioner and acting grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 丙子，契丹主耶律德光卒於鎮之欒城。

translations.literal: On bingzi the Khitan ruler Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng in Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the Khitan ruler Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng in Zhen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽於鎮州自稱權知國事。

translations.literal: At Zhenzhou Zhao Yanshou styled himself acting administrator of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenzhou Zhao Yanshou declared himself acting administrator of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，陜州節度使趙暉加檢校太尉，華州節度使兼陜州馬步軍都指揮使侯章加檢校太傅，以陜府馬步軍副都指揮使兼絳州防禦使王晏為晉州節度使、檢校太傅，以丹州都指揮使、權知軍州事高彥珣為丹州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinsi Zhao Hui, military commissioner of Shaanzhou, was given the additional title of acting Grand Marshal; Hou Zhang, military commissioner of Huazhou and Director-in-Chief of the Shaan horse and foot forces, was given the additional title of acting Grand Tutor; Wang Yan, deputy director of the Shaan horse and foot forces and defense commissioner of Jiangzhou, was made military commissioner of Jinzhou and acting Grand Tutor; and Gao Yancong, director of Danzhou and acting administrator of military and prefectural affairs, was made prefect of Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Shaan commissioner Zhao Hui was made acting grand marshal; Huazhou commissioner and Shaan horse-and-foot commander Hou Zhang, acting grand tutor; Shaan deputy commander and Jiangzhou defense commissioner Wang Yan, Jinzhou military commissioner and acting grand tutor; and acting Danzhou administrator Gao Yancong, Danzhou prefect.
